title: Same $500, four friends: one made $3,650, one made $511,000
question: Same $500. Four friends.
description: A money parable, not a real business and not advice: four friends start with the same $500 and the same coffee. One owns a cart, one rents five, one gets paid a year in advance, one never touches a cup. Four ideas with a name: organic growth, leasing, pre-selling, and a system.

scenes.narration: Same $500. Four friends. One made $3,650. Another made $511,000. Same coffee, same year, same town. Each friend got $500 to start. Here is what each one did.

Friend one bought one coffee cart for exactly $500. He pushes it himself, every morning. It makes about $10 of profit a day. In a year, 365 times $10, that's $3,650. This is called organic growth. Your own money, your own two hands, one cart.

Friend two asked around. Renting a cart costs just $100 a year. So she rented five, with her whole $500. Five carts, 365 days, $10 each, that's $18,250. This is called leasing. You don't need to own the cart to earn from the cart.

Friend three rented five carts too. Then he walked into an office tower and said: buy a year of coffee today, at 80 cents on the dollar, and I deliver every morning. They paid $14,600 up front. With that money he rented 146 more carts. 151 carts, 365 days, $8 each, that's $440,920. This is called pre-selling. The customer's money built the business.

Friend four never bought a cart. She wrote down the recipe, the prices, the rules, and put her name on it. Seventy people now run carts under her name, 20 cups a day each, and pay her $1 a cup. 70 carts, 365 days, 20 cups, $1, that's $511,000. This is called a system. She sells the way to do it, not the coffee.
Same $500. $3,650. $18,250. $440,920. $511,000. The money was the same. The idea was different.
It's a parable, not a plan. But which friend are you? One, two, three, or four? Tell me below, and send this to a friend who still pushes the cart.
Same $500, four very different years. Follow for tomorrow's why.
